ELMALILI:26:69-104/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:69-104/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:69-104/r1.claim: The prayer for a truthful tongue can mean an enduring good name and beautiful remembrance in the world until the Resurrection; every community has loved Abraham.
ELMALILI:26:69-104/r1.anchor: “Lisân-ı sıdk” dünyada kıyamete kadar eseri bâkī kalacak güzel bir nâm, yani bir hüsn-i sıyt, dosdoğru bir zikr-i cemîl, şaşmaz bir yâd-ı hasen; onun için her ümmet Hazret-i İbrâhim’i sevegelmiştir.

ELMALILI:26:69-104/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:69-104/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:69-104/r2.claim: Alternatively, Abraham asks for a truthful voice among his descendants to renew his original religion and call to monotheism; Elmalılı identifies it as Muhammad.
ELMALILI:26:69-104/r2.anchor: Yahut zürriyetim içinde benim asıl dinimi yenileyecek, benim gibi sıdk ile tevhîde davet edecek bir sâdık dil ki Muhammed sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’dir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r1.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r1.claim: One interpretation treats lisān as a metaphor for speech or its transmitters; on this reading Abraham asks that his own words carry true, real, elevated meanings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r1.anchor: Bu tamlamadaki lisân terimi dille aktarılabilecek, dille ulaştırılabilecek şeyleri veya bunları aktaranları ifade için mecaz olarak kullanılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r2.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r2.claim: Another reading of that metaphor takes Abraham's prayer to mean that descendants would transmit his true religion; God answered by sending many prophets from his line, especially Muhammad, and commanding the Prophet to follow Abraham's religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r2.anchor: kendi soyundan, getirmiş olduğu hak dini sonraki nesillere aktaracak kimselerin gelmesini Allah Teâlâ’dan niyaz etmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r3.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r3.claim: A second interpretation is that Abraham asks to be remembered well by later generations; Muslims treat him as a leader and praise him and his descendants, as do Jews and Christians.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r3.anchor: Bu tamlama Hz. İbrâhim’in, sonraki nesiller içerisinde iyilikle anılmak istediğini ifade etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.claim: Exegetes cite various proofs that all of Abraham's requests were granted except his prayer concerning his father.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.anchor: Müfessirler, İbrâhim’in babasının affı dışındaki bütün dileklerinin kabul olunduğuna dair çeşitli deliller getirmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r12.claim: Abraham's prayer for enduring good remembrance was answered: every community loves and praises him, and Muslims name him with the Prophet in the salawat and barakat prayers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r12.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim’in “hep iyilikle anılması” konusundaki duasının bir sonucu olarak her ümmet ona ayrı bir sevgi duymuş ve adını övgüyle anar olmuştur.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r3.claim: Abraham makes this prayer at the sensitive point of declaring acquittal and migrating.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r3.anchor: This is the prayer Abraham (sws) uttered at this sensitive time of his declaration of acquittal and migration.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r6.claim: Lisān means fame or reputation; the construct lisān ṣidq means fond remembrance, more exactly everlasting fond remembrance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r6.anchor: In fact, an accurate translation would be “everlasting fond remembrance.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r7.claim: Abraham asks for broad, lasting acceptance of his message; the prayer was fulfilled through Israelite prophets and ultimately through Muhammad, whose message became global and enduring.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r7.anchor: Finally, Muḥammad, the last of prophet of God, made his message a global and abiding phenomenon.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p167/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p167/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p167/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says لسان الصدق is praise and lasting renown, an interpretation shared by the exegetes; Abraham is honored across religious communities for his monotheism.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p167/r8.anchor: لسان الصدق، قال ابن عطية: هو الثناء وتخليد المكانة بإجماع من المفسرين. وكذلك أجاب الله دعوته، فكل ملة تتمسك به وتعظمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p167/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p167/r9.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p167/r9.claim: Makkī suggests Abraham asked for a descendant in the end times who would uphold truth, fulfilled in Muhammad; the author calls this a good idea but says the wording does not support it without forcing it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p167/r9.anchor: قال مكي: وقيل معنى سؤاله أن يكون من ذريته في آخر الزمان من يقوم بالحق، فأجيبت الدعوة في محمد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r13.claim: “A truthful tongue” means good praise, beautiful remembrance, and broad acceptance among later nations; God granted this, and religious communities praise Abraham.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r13.anchor: أي: ثناء حسنا، وذكرا جميلا وقبولا عاما في الأمم التي تجيء بعدي، فأعطاه الله ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r14.speaker: القتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r14.claim: He says “tongue” metaphorically stands for speech because speech is produced by the tongue.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r14.anchor: وضع اللسان موضع القول على الاستعارة لأن القول يكون به.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r6.claim: A tongue of truth means lasting worldly status and good renown through Judgment, explaining why every nation praises Abraham.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r6.anchor: جاها وحسن صيت في الدنيا يبقى أثره إلى يوم الدين، ولذلك ما من أمة إلا وهم محبون له مثنون عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r7.claim: Alternatively, it asks for a truthful descendant who renews Abraham's religion and calls people to his message: Muhammad.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r7.anchor: أو صادقا من ذريتي يجدد أصل ديني ويدعو الناس إلى ما كنت أدعوهم إليه وهو محمد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r13.claim: A truthful tongue among later people means beautiful remembrance, broad acceptance, and praise for the good God made Abraham display, so he becomes an example for the pious.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r14.claim: The author invokes the saying that one who establishes a good practice earns its reward and the reward of everyone who follows it through the Day of Resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r14.anchor: فإن ( من سن سنة حسنة كان له أجرها وأجر من عمل بها إلى يوم القيامة )

BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r15.claim: God answered by making Abraham a blessed source of prophets who renewed his remembrance, most notably through the Prophet's prayer formula for Muhammad as for Abraham.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r15.anchor: من قوله : ( صل على محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم ) إلى آخره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r5.claim: الصالحين encompasses all righteous people, including prophets and messengers; placing this broad category last makes it a summative tailpiece.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r5.anchor: ولفظ الصالحين يعم جميع الصالحين من الأنبياء والمرسلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r6.claim: The author reads the request as seeking the ranks of the great messengers Nūḥ, Hūd, and Ṣāliḥ, as well as martyrs and the righteous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r6.anchor: فيكون قد سأل بلوغ درجات الرسل أولي العزم نوح وهود وصالح والشهداء والصالحين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r7.claim: Ibrahim asks that later peoples preserve a good reputation for him; this seeks lasting perfection and praise that moves people to pray for him after death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r7.anchor: ثم سأل بقاء ذكر له حسن في الأمم والأجيال الآتية من بعده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r8.claim: God granted his descendants prophets and messengers, so later communities remember Ibrahim and his name endures in scriptures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r8.anchor: وقد جعل الله في ذريته أنبياء ورسلا يذكرونه وتذكره الأمم التابعة لهم ويخلد ذكره في الكتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r9.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r9.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī transmits from Mālik that wanting righteous praise is permissible when one intends God’s pleasure and a good reputation among the righteous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r9.anchor: قال ابن العربي : ( قال مالك : لا بأس أن يحب الرجل أن يثنى عليه صالحا ويرى في عمل الصالحين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r10.claim: The author connects God’s granting Moses love among people with Ibrahim’s request for enduring good remembrance and notes an earlier discussion of the family prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r10.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى : { وألقيت عليك محبة مني } ( طه : 39 )

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r15.claim: The tongue of truth among later generations means praise and lasting honor, by agreement among exegetes; God answered the prayer, and communities honor Abraham while upholding the monotheism brought by Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r15.anchor: و «لسان الصدق» في الآخرين هو الثناء وخلد المكانة بإجماع من المفسرين، وكذلك أجاب الله دعوته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r16.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r16.claim: Makkī offers a further reading: Abraham sought a descendant in the last age who would uphold truth, and the prayer was answered in Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p234#2/r16.anchor: قال مكي وقيل معنى سؤاله أن يكون من ذريته في آخر الزمان من يقوم بالحق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235/r1.claim: The author calls Makkī’s interpretation good but says the wording does not support it without forcing the text.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235/r1.anchor: وهذا معنى حسن إلا أن لفظ الآية لا يعطيه إلا بتحكم على اللفظ

MUQATIL:26:69-85/r15.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r15.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r15.claim: He asks for lasting good praise among later people; God grants this, and people of every religion praise Abraham.
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r15.anchor: يعنى ثناء حسنا يقال: من بعدى فى الناس،

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r1.claim: God's love in people's hearts and their good praise are illustrated by Moses' love and the promise of affection for believers; a truthful tongue asks for lasting good remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r1.anchor: أي حبا في قلوب عباده وثناء حسنا، فنبه تعالى بقوله: { واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين } على استحباب اكتساب ما يورث الذكر الجميل.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r2.speaker: الليث بن سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r2.claim: Al-Layth ibn Sulayman glosses the truthful tongue as the second life.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r2.anchor: الليث بن سليمان: إذ هي الحياة الثانية. قيل: قد مات قوم وهم في الناس أحياء

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says verified Sufi elders find here an encouragement to righteous deeds that earn good praise.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r3.anchor: قال ابن العربي: قال المحققون من شيوخ الزهد في هذا دليل على الترغيب في العمل الصالح الذي يكسب الثناء الحسن،

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r4.claim: The Prophet says a person's deeds cease at death except for three; a report extends the reward for planting and for dying on border duty until Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r4.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا مات ابن آدم انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث " الحديث وفي رواية إنه كذلك في الغرس والزرع

TABATABAI:26:85-89/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r1.claim: The request for a good remembrance among later generations can mean preserving Abraham's call after him by sending messengers like the earlier prophets named in the passage.
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r1.anchor: وقد ذكر هذه الجملة بعد ذكر عدة من الأنبياء غيره كنوح وموسى وهارون وإلياس

TABATABAI:26:85-89/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r2.claim: Another view reads the request as the coming of Muhammad, who reported being the prayer of his father Abraham; the meaning then links to Abraham and Ishmael's prayer for a submitting community and a messenger from among them.
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد به بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وقد روي عنه أنه قال أنا دعوة أبي إبراهيم

TABATABAI:26:85-89/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r3.claim: A further view takes it as beautiful praise and remembrance lasting until Resurrection; the author says that this sense of a true tongue and the equation with Abraham's prayer in al-Baqara are unclear.
TABATABAI:26:85-89/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد به أن يجعل الله له ذكرا جميلا وثناء حسنا بعده إلى يوم القيامة

TABRISI:26:78-84/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r18.claim: A truthful legacy means lasting good praise, remembrance, and acceptance among later generations; all religious communities praise Abraham and acknowledge his prophethood.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r18.anchor: أي ثناء حسنا في آخر الأمم وذكرا جميلا وقبولا عاما في الذين يأتون بعدي إلى يوم القيامة

TABRISI:26:78-84/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r19.claim: Arabs use “tongue” metaphorically for speech and language because speech is made with it; al-Aʿshā's poem illustrates the usage.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r19.anchor: والعرب تضع اللسان موضع القول على الاستعارة لأن القول يكون بها وكذلك يسمون اللغة لسانا قال الأعشى باهلة:

TABRISI:26:85-89/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:85-89/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:26:85-89/r10.claim: Alternatively, Abraham asks for a truthful descendant among later nations who calls people to God and upholds truth: Muḥammad.
TABRISI:26:85-89/r10.anchor: وقيل إن معناه واجعل لي ولد صدق في آخر الأمم يدعو إلى الله ويقوم بالحق وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:77-78/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:77-78/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:77-78/r2.claim: Abraham asks for a good reputation and praise among later generations.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:77-78/r2.anchor: لسان صدق في الآخرين } أي: ذكرا جميلا، وثناء حسنا في الأمم التي تجيء بعدي.

ZAJJAJ:v4p94/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p94/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p94/r1.claim: Abraham asks for lasting, good praise among later generations.
ZAJJAJ:v4p94/r1.anchor: معناه اجعل لي ثناء حسنا باقيا إلى آخر الدهر

ASAD-NOTES:26:83#n39/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:83#n39/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:26:83#n39/r1.claim: The phrase literally asks for a truthful renown or legacy among later people; Asad points to alternative readings in note 36 on 19:50.
ASAD-NOTES:26:83#n39/r1.anchor: Lit., "grant me a language of truth among the others" or "the later ones". For alternative interpretations of this phrase, see note 36 on 19:50.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r1.claim: Ibrahim asks for a truthful, enduring good reputation among all peoples until the Resurrection, gained through good works and approved practices that others follow and praise truthfully.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r1.anchor: اجعل لنفعي ذكرا صادقا في جميع الأمم إلى يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r2.claim: 'Tongue' is a metonym for remembrance by the relation of cause to effect; the lām indicates benefit, and 'the later ones' is universal.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r2.anchor: فاللسان مجاز عن الذكر بعلاقة السببية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r3.claim: The request implicitly seeks success in good works, its true object; it may also seek praise for Ibrahim's conduct, since good praise indicates God's love and approval, which is the ultimate aim.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r3.anchor: والكلام مستلزم لطلب التوفيق للآثار الحسنة التي أشرنا اليها وكأنه المقصود بالطلب على أبلغ وجه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r4.speaker: يحتمل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, 'the later ones' means the final community: Ibrahim seeks a good name among them through a prophet who renews his monotheistic religion, namely Muhammad, as in 2:129 and the hadith 'I am Abraham's prayer.'
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r4.anchor: وأنه عليه السلام طلب الصيت الحسن والذكر الجميل فيهم ببعثه نبي فيهم يجدد أصل دينه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r5.claim: On that alternative, one must supply 'companion of a truthful tongue' or treat the tongue as a part standing for the whole preacher; Al-Alusi says his own account needs neither move.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r5.anchor: فلابد من تقدير مضاف في كلامه عليه السلام أي أجعل لي صاحب لسان صدق

ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r6.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r6.claim: Malik cites the verse to show that it is unobjectionable to wish for people to praise one as righteous.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r6.anchor: واستدل الامام مالك بهذه الآية على أنه لابأس أن يحب الرجل أن يثنى عليه صالحا

ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r7.speaker: بعض الآجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r7.claim: Some scholars say posthumous praise redirects people's efforts toward deeds that bring divine nearness; a good example may prompt imitation and share the reward promised for starting a good practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p98#2/r7.anchor: انصراف الهمم الي ما به يحصل له عند الله تعالى زلفى وأنه قد يصير سببا لاكتساب المثنى

DURR-FULL:v6p306/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets Abraham’s prayer for a truthful reputation among later people to mean every religious community would believe in Abraham.
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين} قال: يؤمن بإبراهيم كل ملة

DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet promises guidance, Paradise food and drink, healing and expiation, blessed life and martyrdom, forgiveness, wisdom, truthful renown, and Paradise homes for one who recites Abraham’s prayer after ablution while leaving for obligatory prayer; al-Ḥasan adds a prayer for the parents.
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا توضأ العبد لصلاة مكتوبة فاسبغ الوضوء

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, interprets the phrase as the agreement of people of all religious communities upon Abraham.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس في قوله : واجعل لي لسان صدق في الاخرين قال : اجتماع اهل الملل على ابراهيم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses «a truthful tongue» as good praise; Qatāda is reported to give the same gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : واجعل لي لسان صدق في الاخرين قال : الثناء الحسن . وروي عن قتادة مثل قول مجاهد

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd explains the phrase as good remembrance, righteous praise, and a good name.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r3.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد في قول الله : واجعل لي لسان صدق في الاخرين قال : اللسان الصدق الذكر والثناء الصالح

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r4.claim: Mujāhid relates the prayer to God’s granting Abraham good in this world, as stated in 16:122.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : واجعل لي لسان صدق في الاخرين قال هو كقوله : واتيناه في الدنيا حسنة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r5.speaker: ليث بن أبي سليم
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r5.claim: Layth ibn Abī Sulaym says people of every religious community believe in Abraham.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r5.anchor: سمعت ليث بن أبي سليم يذكر في قول الله اجعل لي لسان صدق في الاخرين قال : يؤمن به اهل كل ملة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r6.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd glosses «among the later ones» as among later people, with the excerpt’s further wording «من الاسم» left unclear.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2781/r6.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد في قول الله : في الاخرين قال في الاخرين من الناس من الاسم

BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r4.claim: Abraham asks for standing and a good reputation that endures until Judgment; all nations love and praise him.
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r4.anchor: جاها وحسن صيت في الدنيا يبقى أثره إلى يوم الدين ولذلك ما من أمة إلا وهم محبون له مثنون عليه

BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r5.claim: The phrase means good praise and a good name among later peoples; tongue stands for the means by which praise spreads and remembrance lasts.
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r5.anchor: وعبر عن الثناء الحسن والقبول العام باللسان لكون اللسان سببا في ظهوره وانتشاره

BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r6.claim: A lasting good name indicates God's pleasure and love; when God loves a servant, creation, even fish and birds, is made to love him.
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r6.anchor: دولة عظيمة من حيث كونه دليلا على رضى الله عنه ومحبته والله تعالى إذا أحب عبدا يلقي محبته إلى أهل السموات والأرض

BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r7.claim: Ibn Ata reads the prayer as asking that Muhammad's community praise and bear witness for Abraham, since God made them accepted witnesses.
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أي أطلق لسان أمة محمد بالثناء والشهادة لي فإنك قد جعلتهم شداء مقبولين

BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r8.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r8.claim: Sahl says Abraham asks God for praise throughout all nations and religious communities.
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r8.anchor: قال سهل : اللهم ارزقني الثناء في جميع الأمم والملل

BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r9.claim: Good remembrance truly comes through excellent deeds, good character, and a gentle tongue; these prompt later people to follow Abraham, earning him their reward as well.
BURSEVI:v6p207#2/r9.anchor: وإنما يحصل في الحقيقة بالفعل الجميل والخلق الحسن واللسان اللين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#2/r1.claim: The later generations are those who come after Abraham until the Day of Resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#2/r1.anchor: والمراد بالآخرين الذين يأتون بعده إلى يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r9.claim: Abraham asks for a beautiful legacy after his death, so people remember and follow his good example; Ibn Kathir links this to 37:108–110.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r9.anchor: أي: واجعل لي ذكرا جميلا بعدي أذكر به، ويقتدى بي في الخير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r10.claim: Mujahid and Qatada explain the phrase as good praise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد، وقتادة: {واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين} يعني: الثناء الحسن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r11.claim: Mujahid compares the request with God granting Abraham his reward in this world and making him righteous in the next, as stated in 29:27 and 16:122.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد: وهو كقوله تعالى: {وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r12.speaker: ليث بن أبي سليم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r12.claim: Laith ibn Abi Sulaym says every religious community loves Abraham and takes him as an ally; Ikrima agrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147#2/r12.anchor: قال ليث بن أبي سليم: كل ملة تحبه وتتولاه. وكذا قال عكرمة

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r1.claim: Religious argument is valid; truth is known by proof.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r1.anchor: تدل الآية على صحة الحجاج في الدين وأن الحق يعرف بالحجة

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r2.claim: Worship is due to one capable of originating fundamental blessings and controlling benefit and harm.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن العبادة إنما يستحقها القادر على أصول النعم والنفع والضر

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r3.claim: Supplication should begin with monotheism, the prophets' method.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن الأهم في الدعاء البداية بالتوحيد، وهذه طريقة الأنبياء.

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r5.claim: It is good to pray for descendants and an honorable reputation among later generations.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r5.anchor: وتدل على حسن الدعاء للذرية فلذلك قال: (واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين).

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r6.claim: Against natural philosophers, provision and healing come from God; medicine is a cause, while God creates the cure.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن الأرزاق والشفاء منه لا من الدواء خلاف ما تقوله الطبائعية. ومتى قيل: فما معنى الدواء؟ قيل: الدواء سبب الإشفاء، والشفاء من الله تعالى،

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r7.claim: Medicine resembles parents and food: they are causes, while God creates offspring, satiety, and quenching.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r7.anchor: قيل: الدواء سبب الإشفاء، والشفاء من الله تعالى، كما أن الأب والأم سببان والولد خلق لله تعالى، وكما أن الطعام والشراب سببان والشبع والري من الله تعالى،

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r8.claim: Natural causes would yield uniform, undelayed outcomes; nature cannot reason and drugs have no known feature that itself causes healing.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r8.anchor: فليس في الدواء شيء معلوم يحال بالشفاء عليه

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r9.claim: God established habits under which some things nourish, poison, or heal and could have established the opposite.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r9.anchor: ولكن الله تعالى أجرى العادة بأن فعل بعض الأشياء غذاء، وبعضها سما، وبعضها دواء، ولو أجرى العادة على الضد لكان كذلك،

JISHUMI:v7p5369/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r10.claim: Abraham's prayer for his father rested on a promise or rational obligation until he was forbidden.
JISHUMI:v7p5369/r10.anchor: وقد بينا أن دعاءه لأبيه كان لموعدة أو على حكم العقل حتى نهي عنه.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r9.claim: Mujahid and Qatada understand this as giving Abraham good praise among all peoples; “tongue” refers to praise spoken by tongues.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r9.anchor: ثناء حسنا في الأمم كلها , قاله مجاهد , وقتادة , وجعله لسانا لأنه يكون باللسان

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r10.speaker: ليث بن أبي سليم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r10.claim: Layth ibn Abi Sulaym says Abraham asked that people of every religious community believe in him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r10.anchor: أن يؤمن به أهل كل ملة , قاله ليث بن أبي سليم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r11.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r11.claim: Ali ibn Isa reads the prayer as asking for descendants who speak truth after Abraham.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r11.anchor: أن يجعل من ولده من يقول بالحق بعده , قاله علي بن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r12.claim: Al-Mawardi allows that Abraham be affirmed as truthful among all religious communities, and says this prayer was answered.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r12.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أن يكون مصدقا في جمع الملل وقد أجيب إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#5/r1.claim: Abraham asks for good praise and beautiful remembrance among later peoples; God granted it and people of every religion honor and praise him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#5/r1.anchor: أى ثناء حسنا وذكرا جميلا فى الأمم التى تجئ بعدى فأعطى ذلك فكل أهل دين يتولونه ويثنون عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#5/r2.claim: Tongue stands for speech because speech is produced by the tongue.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#5/r2.anchor: ووضع اللسان موضع القول لأن القول يكون به

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the phrase as the nations' gathering around Abraham.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو اجتماع الأمم عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r7.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r7.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as good praise.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says it is good praise and a lasting honored place, the commentators' consensus; every nation holds to and honors Abraham's hanīf way, brought by Muḥammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هو الثناء وخلد المكانة بإجماع المفسرين وكذلك أجاب الله دعوته، وكل أمة تتمسك به وتعظمه، وهو على الحنيفية التي جاء بها محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r9.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r9.claim: Makkī suggests Abraham asked for a later descendant upholding truth, answered by Muḥammad; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is good but the wording does not support it without forcing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r9.anchor: وقال مكي: وقيل معناه سؤاله أن يكون من ذريته في آخر الزمان من يقوم بالحق فأجيبت الدعوة في محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r10.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r10.claim: Al-Qushayrī takes the request as a good prayer lasting until the Resurrection, since increased reward is sought by everyone.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r10.anchor: وقال القشيري: أراد الدعاء الحسن إلى قيام الساعة فإن زيادة الثواب مطلوبة في حق كل أحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r11.claim: Qurṭubī says the prayer was answered: blessings on Muḥammad include blessings on Abraham, especially in prayers and from pulpits.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r11.anchor: قلت: وقد فعل الله ذلك إذ ليس أحد يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا وهو يصلي على إبراهيم وخاصة في الصلوات، وعلى المنابر التي هي أفضل الحالات وأفضل الدرجات.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r12.claim: Lisān means speech here; the tongue is the speech organ, and prayer means supplication for mercy.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r12.anchor: والصلاة دعاء بالرحمة: والمراد باللسان القول، وأصله جارحة الكلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r13.speaker: القتبي
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r13.claim: Al-Qutaybī says the tongue's place stands metaphorically for speech, and Arabs use lisān for a word or expression.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r13.anchor: قال القتبي: وموضع اللسان موضع القول على الاستعارة، وقد تكني العرب بها عن الكلمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r14.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r14.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line uses lisān for a message or report from above; it concerned news of his brother's killing.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r14.anchor: قال الأعشى: إني أتتني لسان لا أسر بها من علو لا عجب منها ولا سخر

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r15.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r15.claim: Al-Jawharī records three vocalizations of ʿulū; the line means news from above, with feminine agreement for the word.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r15.anchor: قال الجوهري: يروى من علو بضم الواو وفتحها وكسرها. أي أتاني خبر من أعلى، والتأنيث للكلمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r16.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r16.claim: Mālik says a person may wish for righteous praise and to be seen among doers of good if he seeks God's pleasure.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-84/r16.anchor: روى أشهب عن مالك قال قال الله عز وجل: { واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين } لا بأس أن يحب الرجل أن يثنى عليه صالحا ويرى في عمل الصالحين،

QASHANI:26:83-84/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:83-84/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:83-84/r2.claim: God makes him beloved, so creation loves him through God's love and remembers him favorably across generations; mentioning remembrance stands for the thing remembered.
QASHANI:26:83-84/r2.anchor: إذ لا بد لمن يحب شيئا من كثرة ذكره بالخير ذكر اللازم مكان الملزوم

QASHANI:26:83-84/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:83-84/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:83-84/r4.claim: The prophets in this chapter can each symbolize spirit or heart, while their people's denial symbolizes the soul's powers refusing spiritual discipline and the morals of perfected people.
QASHANI:26:83-84/r4.anchor: يمكن أن يؤول كل نبي مذكور فيها بالروح أو القلب

QASHANI:26:83-84/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:83-84/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:83-84/r5.claim: In this allegory, the prophet's call to fear God means avoiding vices, and being a trustworthy messenger means conveying received certain truths without admixture of illusion or fantasy.
QASHANI:26:83-84/r5.anchor: أؤدي إليكم ما تلقفت من الحق من الحكم والمعاني اليقينية غير مخلوطة بالوهميات والتخيلات

RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r1.claim: Rāzī reads Abraham’s sequence as seeking knowledge first, then worldly perfections: inward virtue rather than outward appearance, and spiritual honor and lasting remembrance rather than wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r1.anchor: ابتدأ بطلب ما هو الكمال الذاتي للإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r2.claim: He explains the wish for praise in two ways: gathered human attention may increase a person’s perfection, and public praise of virtue can inspire others to acquire the same virtues.
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r2.anchor: إذا اجتمعت طائفة منها فربما قوي مجموعها على ما عجزت الآحاد عنه

RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God granted Abraham this lasting good mention, as confirmed by the statement that his good name was left among later generations.
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وقد أعطاه

RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r4.claim: A second interpretation is that Abraham asks for a truthful caller to God among later generations, namely Muhammad; the phrase thus refers to Muhammad’s mission.
RAZI-FULL:v24p129/r4.anchor: من ذريته في آخر الزمان من يكون داعيا إلى الله تعالى

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r1.claim: One reported sense is that religious communities will unite around Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r1.anchor: religious communities will unite around Abraham

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r2.claim: Another reported sense is Abraham being praised beautifully and holding high rank for all time.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r2.anchor: he will be praised beautifully and have high rank for all time

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r3.claim: Another reported sense is that Abraham's descendants uphold the truth to the end of time.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r3.anchor: he will have descendants who will uphold the truth until the end of time

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r4.claim: Another reported sense is Abraham asking for prayers on his behalf until Judgment Day.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r4.anchor: he desires prayers on his behalf until the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r5.claim: Lisān literally means tongue, though some take it to mean word; here it is rendered renown.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r5.anchor: Renown renders lisān, which literally means

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r6.claim: Ṣidq can mean sincere or true.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r6.anchor: faithful renders ṣidq, which can also mean

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r7.claim: The core sense is Abraham's wish for good, sincere words to be spoken on his behalf.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r7.anchor: the core meaning here is that Abraham desires that good and sincere words be uttered on his behalf

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r8.claim: R interprets the prayer as asking for good qualities worthy of remembrance in later times.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r8.anchor: good qualities that would be worthy of remembrance in later times (R)

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r9.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r9.claim: Ṭ understands Abraham to ask not to be lied about in later generations.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r9.anchor: he desires not to be lied about in later times (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r10.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r10.claim: Q and R understand the prayer as fulfilled in Muhammad, Abraham's descendant who calls people to God.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r10.anchor: a descendant who would call others to God (Q, R)

STUDYQURAN:26:84/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r11.claim: The prayer can be seen as fulfilled in 19:50.
STUDYQURAN:26:84/r11.anchor: see also 19:50, which can in a sense be seen as a fulfillment of this prayer

TAB-FULL:v17p593/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r3.claim: Abraham asks for a beautiful, good reputation that endures among people of later generations.
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r3.anchor: وقوله: {واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين} [الشعراء: 84] يقول: واجعل لي في الناس ذكرا جميلا

TAB-FULL:v17p593/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r4.claim: Ikrima says Abraham asked that later nations would not deny him; God granted this lasting recognition.
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r4.anchor: عن أبي بكر، عن عكرمة، قوله: " {واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين}

TAB-FULL:v17p593/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r5.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r5.claim: Ikrima explains that Jews believed Moses but rejected Jesus, Christians believed Jesus but rejected Muhammad, yet each community claimed Abraham.
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r5.anchor: عن أبي بكر، عن عكرمة، قوله: " {واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين}

TAB-FULL:v17p593/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r6.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r6.claim: Ikrima says the Jews claimed Abraham as their intimate friend and ancestor, but God denied that he was Jewish or Christian and assigned his allegiance to Muhammad and the believers.
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r6.anchor: عن أبي بكر، عن عكرمة، قوله: " {واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين}

TAB-FULL:v17p593/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r7.claim: Ikrima identifies this as Abraham's reward and the good granted him in worldly life, a lasting reputation among later peoples.
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r7.anchor: عن أبي بكر، عن عكرمة، قوله: " {واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين}

TAB-FULL:v17p593/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses this as truthful remembrance and good praise that endures among later peoples.
TAB-FULL:v17p593/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين} [الشعراء: 84]

SULAMI:v2p77#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p77#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p77#4/r1.claim: Abraham asks that Muhammad’s community be given tongues to praise and testify for him, since God made them accepted witnesses.
SULAMI:v2p77#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : أطلق ألسنة أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالثناء

SULAMI:v2p77#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p77#4/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p77#4/r2.claim: Abraham asks for praise among all nations and dominions.
SULAMI:v2p77#4/r2.anchor: قال سهل : ارزقني الثناء في جميع الأمم والملك

TUSTARI:26:84/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:26:84/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:26:84/r1.claim: The prayer asks God to grant Abraham praise among all peoples and assemblies.
TUSTARI:26:84/r1.anchor: ارزقني الثناء في جميع الأمم والملأ

TABATABAI:26:83-84/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib contrasts ṣalāḥ with fasād: it is remaining according to one’s original nature so that its proper good effects arise without corruption.
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r3.anchor: الصلاح - على ما ذكره الراغب - يقابل الفساد

TABATABAI:26:83-84/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r4.claim: The righteous here are sound in their essence, not merely in deeds: they are fully prepared for divine mercy and every good, unhindered by corrupt belief or action; essential righteousness follows the gift of wisdom.
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r4.anchor: فالمراد به الصالحون ذاتا لا عملا فحسب وإن كان صلاح الذات لا ينفك عنه صلاح العمل

TABATABAI:26:83-84/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r5.claim: Joining the righteous follows from receiving wisdom: Abraham’s request means, “Grant me wisdom and complete its effect in me, namely essential righteousness.” The author links this to 16:122.
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r5.anchor: فمسألته الإلحاق بالصالحين من لوازم مسألة موهبة الحكم وفروعها المترتبة عليها

TABATABAI:26:83-84/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r6.claim: The possessive construction “tongue of truth” makes the tongue exclusively truthful, speaking only what is in its owner’s heart.
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r6.anchor: إضافة اللسان إلى الصدق لامية تفيد اختصاصة بالصدق بحيث لا يتكلم إلا به

TABATABAI:26:83-84/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r7.claim: Abraham asks God to raise later generations who continue his mission and call people to his monotheistic religion.
TABATABAI:26:83-84/r7.anchor: فيؤول المعنى إلى مسألة أن يبعث الله في الآخرين من يقوم بدعوته ويدعو الناس إلى ملته

THALABI:v7p170/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p170/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p170/r2.claim: Abraham asks for beautiful remembrance, praise, and broad acceptance among later peoples; God granted it, and religious communities honor him and build upon his legacy.
THALABI:v7p170/r2.anchor: أي ذكرا جميلا وثناء حسنا وقبولا عاما في الأمم

THALABI:v7p170/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p170/r3.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v7p170/r3.claim: Al-Qutaybi says tongue stands metaphorically for speech, which is alluded to by the tongue, and Arabs also call a language a tongue; al-A'sha al-Bahili's line uses lisan for a message or speech.
THALABI:v7p170/r3.anchor: قال القتيبي: ووضع اللسان موضع القول على الاستعارة لأن القول يكنى بها

THALABI:v7p170/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p170/r4.speaker: الأعشى الباهلي
THALABI:v7p170/r4.claim: Al-A'sha al-Bahili's verse uses lisan for a spoken message that arrives from a distant source.
THALABI:v7p170/r4.anchor: وقال أعشى باهلة: إني أتتني لسان لا أسر بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، سفيان، السدي، مقاتل، الكلبي، المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r1.claim: They explain لسان صدق as good praise among generations that come after Abraham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وسفيان، والسدي، ومقاتل، والكلبي، والمفسرون يعني: ثناء حسنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r2.claim: The later generations are those who come after Abraham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r2.anchor: {في الآخرين} يعني: في الذين يأتون بعدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the prayer asks for good praise lasting until the end of time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معناه اجعل لي ثناء حسنا باقيا إلى آخر الدهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r4.claim: The commentators say God granted the prayer: people of every religion cherish and praise Abraham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: وأعطاه الله ذلك، وكل أهل دين يتولونه ويثنون عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r5.claim: Tongue can stand for speech, as in the cited line إني أتتني لسان.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r5.anchor: وذكرنا أن اللسان قد يذكر والمراد به القول (¬3)، ومنه:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r6.claim: Arabs attach صِدق to a praised thing, as in قدم صدق in Yūnus 10:2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p72#2/r6.anchor: والعرب إذا مدحت شيئا أضافته إلى الصدق (¬5)؛ كقوله تعالى: {قدم صدق}

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p508/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p508/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p508/r5.claim: Abraham asks for lasting good repute among later generations; people of every religion love him, as in the statement that God left praise for him among later peoples.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p508/r5.anchor: في الآخرة، فليس من أهل دين إلا وهم يتولونه ويحبونه، وهي مثل قوله: {وتركنا عليه في الآخرين}

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r2.claim: The tongue can stand for speech; Abraham's لسان صدق means good remembrance, while a poet uses لسان for unwelcome news.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r2.anchor: ومن الاستعارة: اللسان يوضع موضع القول، لأن القول يكون بها.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r3.speaker: شاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses لسان to mean a report or news that brings no pleasure.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر : إني أتتني لسان لا أسر بها ...

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p59/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p59/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p59/r1.claim: He invokes a truthful legacy among later people while arguing that scholarly investigation is needed to uncover hidden meanings in proverbs, idioms, and transmitted reports.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p59/r1.anchor: لولا العلماء المنقبون في البلاد، المنقرون عن الخبء، الناظرون للخلوف،

DAMGHANI:v1p413/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p413/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p413/r11.claim: Lisān can mean a good or honorable mention among later generations.
DAMGHANI:v1p413/r11.anchor: الرابع : اللسان الثناء الحسن قوله سبحانه في سورة الشعراء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p533/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p533/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p533/r5.claim: Lisān can mean good praise or favorable mention among later generations.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p533/r5.anchor: والرابع : الثناء الحسن . ومنه قوله تعالى في الشعراء
